question.text: This Spaniard led the war against the Incas and ordered the execution of Atahualpa, even though Atahualpa offered to give this man a room filled with gold.
question.clue: This man received help from longtime partner Diego Almagro, but he was killed by Almagro's forces in the Battle of Las Salinas.

swap.leadin: This man fought Huascar (WAHS-car) during the War of the Two Brothers.
swap.text: Name this ruler who was strangled at the hands of Spanish conquistadors after converting to Christianity. He lost his capital of Cuzco to the Spanish when he failed to fill a room with gold.
swap.clue: He offered to fill a large room with gold and silver for his ransom, but the Spaniards didn't release him.

question.text: Timur allegedly built pyramids out of these body parts, the protective structure for the brain, which would terrify his enemies.
question.clue: After sacking Ankara in Turkey, Tamerlane allegedly made a pyramid of these objects.

swap.leadin: Like the related Aymaras, the women of this ethnic group often wear bowler hats.
swap.text: Identify this ethnic group that is indigenous to the Andes. The language of this ethnic group was used by the Incans to record messages on quipus.
swap.answerHtml: Quechua [accept more specific groups such as Runakuna, Kichwas, or Ingas]
swap.clue: The MUPP-NP party's common name is a word in this language that's gained popularity with indigenists for its connotation of "world reversal."

question.leadin: The "trophy heads" collected by this culture featured a hole in the skull where a rope was threaded through.
question.text: Name this culture who created geoglyphs in the shape of condors and hummingbirds in the desert, known as their namesake "lines."
question.clue: This culture built the Cantalloc ("cahn-TAH-yoke")Aqueducts, exemplifying the corkscrew entrances of their puquios ("poo-KEE-ohʼs").

swap.leadin: In its native Quechua tongue it is known as Tawantinsuyu or "Land of the Four Quarters"
swap.text: Identify this empire conquered by the Spanish and whose mita system was used by the Spanish to run the silver mines at Potosi.
swap.clue: After the Battle of Cajamarca , Atahualpa was captured and executed by Francisco Pizarro, ending this polity.

question.leadin: This country is home to a Maoist cell called Shining Path, whose crackdown led to many human rights abuses by its ethnically Japanese president Alberto Fujimori in the 90s.
question.text: Name this country whose navy was beaten by nearby Chile in the War of the Pacific. This country just got back a trove of artifacts that Yale stole from Machu Picchu.
question.clue: That culture in this country was also responsible for creating a series of images called Lines near Palpa that are well-known geoglyphs.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about European relations with the New World FTPE.
swap.text: The Incas fought a disastrous battle with this Spanish conquistador at Cajamarca in 1532.
swap.clue: This leader of the "famous thirteen" ambushed a certain opponent at Cajamarca and retrieved twenty-four tons of gold and silver after ordering a room to be filled with precious metal.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Inca emperor Atahualpa.
question.text: After the death of his father Huayna Capac, Atahualpa fought this brother for control of the Inca Empire. He was defeated and imprisoned after losses at Chimborazo and Quipaipan.
question.clue: This Peruvian ship sank the Esmeralda before Chile captured it in the War of the Pacific. It took its name from an Incan noble who lost a civil war to his brother Atahualpa.

swap.text: The Nazca were based in this country. The Incan capital Cuzco was located in this country.
swap.clue: Shining Path was opposed by this country's Grupo Colina death squad, which was overseen by its longtime autocratic president Alberto Fujimori.

question.text: Conquistadors high off chivalric fantasies searched for this mythical city of gold inspired by Muisca folklore.
question.clue: During the first part of the journey in which Orellana travelled the length of the Amazon, a valley of Cinnamon and this place were the targets of Gonzalo Pizzaro.

swap.text: This Inca city was shaped like a puma and served as the capital of the empire. Legend holds that it was built by Pachacuti.
swap.clue: Juan Veramendi erected a Basilica Cathedral here, and Vicente Valverde served as the first bishop of this city, where Diego Almagro was executed.

question.leadin: These structures were first described as trail markers in the 1553 Cronicas del Peru by Pedro Cieza de Leon.
question.text: Name these geoglyphs found in their namesake desert in southern Peru that include a hummingbird and spider. Some people think that aliens made these geoglyphs, as they can only be seen in full from above.
question.clue: These things were damaged by Greenpeace activists wearing improper footwear as part of a 2014 protest.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about undeciphered writing systems.
swap.text: The exact meaning of this system of knot-writing from the Incan empire is still unknown. This system may have been used to record the Aymara and Quechua spoken languages.
swap.clue: This objects that were used for record-keeping and other purposes by the Inca.

question.leadin: Structures built by this civilization shared many commonalities with ritual centers built in the contemporary Kotosh religious tradition style.
question.text: Name this ancient civilization in modern-day Peru, the oldest-known civilization in the Americas. The MFAC theory regarding the beginning of this civilization has been heavily undermined by further excavation.

swap.leadin: These people invented one of the first medium distance communication systems with two resin-coated gourds connected by a 75m length of twine.
swap.text: Name these people who had their capital at Chan Chan and who made use of the Spondylus shellfish and produced notably black shiny pottery.
swap.clue: These people succeeded the Moche, and they ruled from their capital at Chan Chan.

question.leadin: Father Jose Domingo Duquesne ("dew-CANE") was tasked with studying these people's namesake language, which was also called Chibcha.
question.text: Name these people governed in the north by zaques ("SAH-kays") and in the south by zipas ("SEE-pahs") until conquistadors invaded their "confederation."
question.clue: This people, who mined salt in large gacha pots and imported gold for tunjo figures of humans or animals at Guatavita.

swap.text: During his invasion of Upper Peru, Belgrano set up his auxiliary base in this city. The "Real Situado" was an annual payment of silver from the rich mines of this city, where Cerro Rico was discovered in 1545 by a native Quechua Indian.
swap.answerHtml: <u>Potosí</u> [do not accept or prompt on “San Luis Potosí”]
swap.clue: Workers in this city still give offerings to a goat-headed underworld deity called "The Uncle" or El Tio.

question.leadin: Along with the Chavin culture, this culture was investigated by Julio Tello, who found hundreds of "mummy bundles" on a peninsula that shares this culture's name.
question.text: Name this culture that built a necropolis at its site of Wari Kayan. This Andean culture in modern-day Peru strongly influenced its successor, the Nazca culture.

swap.leadin: In the best-known version of the Inkarri myth, a man with this name will be resurrected to throw off European rule.
swap.text: Give this name of the last ruler of a state defeated by Viceroy Francisco de Toledo. A later rebel adopted this name during his fight against the Bourbon Reforms.
swap.answerHtml: Túpac Amaru [accept Topa Amaru; accept Thupaq Amaru; accept Amaro in place of “Amaru”; accept José Gabriel Túpac Amaru II; accept José Gabriel Condorcanqui Noguera; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: The legitimate son of Manco Capac, he was captured an executed for the death of Friar Diego Ortiz.
